title: Introduce scratchpad prefetch attention kernel and shared KV ring-buffer with scheduler hints
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a new attention microkernel that uses on-chip scratchpad prefetching and a shared KV ring-buffer to reduce memory stalls. Exposes a lightweight scheduler hint API to improve continuous batching coalescing. Performance: +15-28% throughput on long-context workloads and p95 latency improvements on heavy concurrent workloads.
description:
Motivation: Long-context attention workloads suffer from DRAM stalls when streaming KV cache for many concurrent in-flight requests. Existing continuous-batcher coalescing helps but loses effectiveness when KV lifetime varies across requests. This PR introduces a new attention microkernel that uses an on-chip scratchpad prefetch loop plus a shared ring-buffer-backed KV cache to reduce DRAM traffic and overlap compute with scatter-prefetch. We also expose a minimal scheduler hint API so the continuous batcher can group requests by expected KV-lifetime and prefetch priority.

What this does (high level):
- Adds src/runtime/attn/scratchpad_kernel.*: a CUDA implementation that allocates per-warp scratchpad lanes, prefetches blocks of KV in an interleaved fashion, and streams them into registers to minimize global memory wait. Kernel falls back to existing fastpath for small sequence lengths.
- Introduces a shared KV ring-buffer (src/runtime/kv/ring_buffer_cache.*) that allows multiple concurrent requests to share resident KV slices rather than duplicating copies per-stream. The ring buffer adds a lightweight refcount and eviction callback for late arrivals.
- Scheduler hint API (src/runtime/scheduler/hinting_api.*) with two calls: hint_prefetch_priority(request_id, priority_hint) and hint_kv_lifetime(request_id, lifetime_bucket). The continuous batcher uses these to coalesce and order work to maximize reuse.
- Perf tests and benchmarks + docs and a recipe demonstrating config knobs for prefetch depth and ring-buffer size.

Checklist: [x] Kernel design and smoke tests [x] Ring-buffer implementation and unit tests [x] Scheduler hint API + integration with continuous_batcher [x] Benchmarks showing improvement [x] Documentation and recipe [x] CI green (after one flaky perf rerun)

Benchmarks / Results:
- Long-context (16k token) streaming generation, 8 concurrent clients: end-to-end tokens/sec +18-22% (median across GPUs tested), p95 latency reduced ~12%.
- Medium-context (4k token) with high concurrency: tokens/sec +15% with ring-buffer enabled; additional +3-6% with kernel prefetching enabled.
- Memory: peak device DRAM pressure reduced ~20% in shared-KV scenarios due to deduplication in ring buffer.
- Microbenchmarks: kernel arithmetic throughput matches previous fastpath for short sequences; benefits appear at sequence lengths >= 1024 and when KV lifetimes overlap.

Commits (summary):
- feat(attn): add scratchpad prefetch attention kernel and integration hooks
- feat(kv): implement ring-buffer-backed shared KV cache with eviction 
- feat(scheduler): add hinting API and continuous-batcher integration
- test: add unit and perf tests for kernel + ring buffer
- docs: add design notes and benchmark recipe

Small illustrative diff snippet: src/runtime/attn/scratchpad_kernel.cu: 
- for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) { load(kv[i]); compute(); }
+ // interleaved prefetch lanes into scratchpad; overlap loads with compute
+ for (int lane = 0; lane < PREFETCH_LANES; ++lane) { prefetch_to_scratch(lane, kv_offset + lane * STRIDE); }
+ __syncthreads();
+ for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) { consume_from_scratch(i); compute(); }

Integration and testing notes: The ring-buffer is optional and can be toggled via runtime flag "--kv-shared-ring=true". Default is off for compatibility. The scheduler hint API is backwards compatible: when no hints are provided the continuous batcher will behave as before. The PR adds a small migration note in docs advising operators to tune ring-buffer capacity by working-set size.

Risks and mitigations:
- Eviction races: addressed with atomic refcounts and an eviction callback that pins in-flight slices. Unit and stress tests simulate high churn.
- Regressions on short-context workloads: kernel falls back to existing path unless sequence length passes threshold or explicit config enables it. Tests ensure parity for small sequences.

Next steps: explore automatic lifetime inference from token histograms, add eviction-aware scheduling policies, and upstream an optimized memcpy variant used by the ring buffer.
commits_summary: 5 commits: add new CUDA kernel (scratchpad prefetch), implement shared ring-buffer cache with eviction/refcount, scheduler hints and integration, perf tests, docs and CI updates.
review_comments: Ada Lin: Looks good overall. Two concerns: 1) ring-buffer refcounting needs a comment explaining the race window; 2) please add a perf check gating to avoid false negatives on CI (we saw a flake).
Priya Nair: Response: added detailed comment in ring_buffer_cache.h and introduced a CI perf-check threshold that tolerates small variance. Also added stress test for refcount races.
Samir Patel: Could we expose a knob for maximum prefetched bytes per request? Otherwise lgtm after small nits.
Priya Nair: Added prefetched_bytes_limit config in examples/recipes and a runtime env var REDWOOD_PREFETCH_BYTES. Addressed style nit and rebased onto main.
Jonah Reed: Approving — benchmark numbers look solid and fallbacks are safe. CI green after rerun.
